Richmond – Refuel; Refresh and Re-Invent

By: Diana Lucas | Commission

Proposal


Show:

Summary:
Richmond, for years simply a place to stretch your legs, refuel and grab a snack before you continue your journey through the Karoo.

Richmond lies just off the N1, between Johannesburg and Cape Town. It’s the signs to the dorp, that litter the NI, that are more obvious then the town- that is until you turn off the tar and enter Richmond wonderland.

Loop Street with its picture perfect converted houses and B and B’s.

There is a rich saddle horse history in the Richmond area. The earliest settlers, called Trekboers, had spent a lifetime in their saddles, and were among the best horsemen in the world. When diamonds were discovered, opportunities abounded for breeding carriage and draught horses, and for carting goods around the area. -The Horse Museum, in Loop Streett one of only two of its kind dedicated to the riding horse. . Johan Tolkien is the curator.

Richmond was occupied by the English in the Anglo Boer war and under attack from Boer troops in Bloemfontein. Fort Vegkop , known to British as Flaghill to the Boers as Flagkop, Is the fort British soldiers would defend their occupation of Richmond. John Donaldson owner of Richmond Books and Prints – specialises in the history of the Anglo Boer War.


Further information:
The nearest blockhouse is 40 kms away by Meriman Siding. ( Railway line).

Right next door to the Horse Museum is another museum with a collection of interesting relics like, Anglo-Boer War gravestones; a relic from the old cooldrink factory; cuttings about an infamous local murder, a collection of vinyl albums of popular music from 50 years ago and an enormous whale vertebra,
Further on along Loop Street is the reading room for the Bookbedonnerd Literary Festival, which takes place every October. The festival has featured literary notables like Athol Fugard; Professor Jonathan Jansen, Riaan Malan and Breyten Breytenbach over the past decade.
A classic old brickworks,
a bar with saddles for seats,
Die Vetmuis restaurant started by four farm women and a Supper club, Die Supper Klub owned by a man who comes from Canada.
With all that going on an extra ordinary feature of this little karoo dorp is the visually stunning MAPSA gallery with t’s large collection of modern and contemporary South African art.
Part of the gallery is a book-binding centre, where a team of Richmond community women produce works of art in book form, using Japanese paper craft techniques to bind pages into books, covered in recycled flour, maize and sugar bags. ( if we send them our Carte Blanche logo they will create a wood cut)
The brains behind this Modern Art Project is Harrie Siertsema and Pretoria-born, Berlin based artist and curator Abrie Fourie… both of them travel throughout the year but will be there on the May the first weekend.
Another person who has found her own creative haven in the dorp is Lientjie Wessels, one of SA’s best chef’s or food artists . She will have a pop up food table on that weekend.
Aubrey Williams and his husband created Karoo Creations during COVID when their Richmond Small Hotel was forced to shut it’s doors. To feed themselves and keep their staff in jobs they transformed their hotel into Karoo Creations, which produces top-end duvets made from sheep’s wool.
“So, we were like, what can we do? Well we’re in the middle of sheep country, so we sourced around and found a supplier for wool that was still operating. We got a fabric supplier and started making duvets, and, ja, it took off like rockets
At the edge of town is the Hope Centre, which feeds more than 200 Richmond children on most weekdays
This is just a sample of what’s on offer in the dorp. The weekend 1st, 2nd and 3rd of May would be the perfect time to film, the town will be alive and vibrant with social and cultural hapenings and people. A good time for filming some essential interviews mixed with off the cuff people and events we come across.

Script:


Mac: Nothing cooler than a road trip and the long stretch of the N1 heading into the Karoo into almost nowhere. But, this time we’re going to Richmond.
V/O
Richmond, a small dorpie in the Northern Cape.
For years simply a pit stop for a quick refuel - a coke or coffee - and you’re back on the road…..
Mac: You’re saying there are a lot of stories about this here?
John: Yes
V/O
But this is a town steeped in history. ….
Mac: Going up here, carrying a rifle.
V/O
A small hill known as Fort Vegkop, is the ideal place to get the lay of the land.
`Mac So this was the old lookout point.
V/O
The town was garrisoned by the British in the Anglo Boer of 1901….Boer rebels attacked Richmond twice….but were successfully repulsed by British Forces.
Mac: So where were the Boers coming from?
John The second onslaught on Richmond, they entered town from the West
Link: When you’re standing up here you can understand why the British would have used it as their Vantage point because you’ve got a total view of what’s happening throughout and around Richmond.
V/O
And these days, there a surprising amount happening. We’re seeking out the people breathing new life into the dorp.
Lientjie Wessels: So it’s art and a book town and some great people around, and it’s the Karoo,so beautiful.
Mac: What more can you ask for right.
Lientjie: Ya Absolutely
V/O
Artist, chef… and relative newcomer Lientjie Wessels is launching Richmond’s Karoo Market. …
Lientjie: We need to get more people into town and to create better opportunities for everybody and that was the idea of the market is to have a real community market and this is our first one
Mac So we are here at the first one?
Lientjie: it’s the first one.
Mac: The inauguration of the Karoo mark..
Lientjie Ya
VO: Loop Street, is the heart of the town. And it’s where Harrie Siertsema spotted a for-sale sign on a rundown house in 2007.
Harrie’s no stranger to road trips. His iconic pancake parlour, Harrie’s Pancakes, is an essential part of many a drive through Mpumalanga.
Mac: On my way to Gods Window and all of that…Harrie’s Pancakes, Pancakes and when I got there and then I think I had that salmon one and I was hooked.
VO: Harrie’s new house came with a supermarket – and the supermarket… became an art gallery.
Harri: The first thing I did before I even baked a pancake in any of those venues, was to hang an art work. That’s my passion, that’s my life.
Mac: This is cool, this is really cool.
V/O
This is our biggest surprise …a warehouse of modern and contemporary art.
Mac: Good to meet you .. is this your space here?
Abri: It’s Modern Art Projects, South Africa.
Mac Unbelievable I’ve been to Art Galleries but this is incredible.
V/O
Berlin based artist Abri Fourie curates this eclectic collection.
Mac: I’ll hold this, I’ll hold this. I will lift it up a little bit
….. I am an Art handler guys please respect me… art handler!
V/O
Modern Art Projects or MAPSA ‘s mission is to promote and support contemporary art in South Africa.
Link: I think for me the most amazing thing about all of this is how simple everyday objects have just been taken and turned into pieces of art.
Mac: Do some shopping with this hey?
V/O
Abri sources pieces all over South Africa, from young art students and well, known artists… it’s all thrown into the mix.
Mac: What I found very interesting that as much as there is a lot of contemporary art in this space right? There is also social statements that are being made by a lot of the art.
Abri: I think there is sense of pure chance but there is beauty in everything, in a sense, right? So it doesn’t have to be a beautiful flower, if you look at a dead donkey it’s not exactly the most beautiful sight. We have a problem, of course, because we keep adding things.
V/O
The gallery’s utterly modern collection is a dramatic contrast to the town’s older curiosities – like Richmond Prints and Books. It's owned by John Donaldson, our guide on the Fort Vegkop hike.
…. Room after Room of books, around 30 000 at his last count.
V/O
The most valuable? Congo by acclaimed, South African Artist Irma Stern…. at R 15 000.
John: Only 300 copies were printed in 1943.
Mac: Looks like such a simple book but it’s just sought after?
John: Yes, they all look different because the cover was handmade, so you don’t get two copies identical.
V/O
But what catches my eye is reading matter of a very different kind.
Mac: These I also used to collect growing up, they were also very sought after in High School because I was a boarding school boy. Where do you get these?
John: This is a Scope magazine for those that don’t know, it used to be South Africa’s version of playboy…
Mac: Yes
John It was occasionally banned by the authorities, for their erotic content.
Mac: There is nothing erotic here, for the times that we’re living in .. they are very well dressed.
Mac And are all these for sale or is this just for collection?
John: It’ for sale
Mac: Aah well thank you. You’ll let me know how much these copies are.
V/O
Richmond offers another way of life – that, and a small hotel for sale, is what lured Aubrey and his husband Lionel to the town.
Aubrey; So what we wanted to do with the hotel was bring back the original feeling, three course dinners on a Sunday with the waiters with…..
Mac: With the butler?
Aubrey: Almost Ya
Mac: Then came Covid that tripped all of us?
Aubrey: We had to refund all the guests that booked with us. And after all the refunds were done we literally had R 1 300 left in the bank.
Mac Weren’t you scared?
Aubrey: If you are on the edge of a cliff you can either jump and fall or you can fly,
V/O
Maybe it was the creative spirit of Richmond – or maybe it was the ever-present Karoo sheep – that inspired them to make wool duvets. Either way, Karoo Creations was born.
Aubrey: It was blood sweat, tears, ,literally. I knew how to work a very small sewing machine, everything else was Youtubed and, googled.
V/O
This month, Karoo Creations moved into bigger premises - From a team of two Aubrey and John now have 18 people working for them
Aubrey: Everybody that joined us was previously unemployed We have trained people up. We cannot do what we do without our team.
V/O
The businesses moving into Richmond bring jobs. The guesthouses and restaurants teach new skills – and MAPSA has opened a book-binding centre.
Link You’ve done a great one here I can see this one this is their best work of art so far they have never done anything as beautiful as this so thank you here we go can you see. Best work of art
V/O
And the most attractive dustbins in South Africa are being installed around the town.
V/O
Even long-gone residents make the odd appearance, it seems – at this former orphanage, now one of only two Horse Museums in the world.

Mac: It was in this room where the spook action happened.

V/O
Curator Johan Tolken says it was ten years ago that he became aware of their presence.

Johan: (SUBS) A friend and I came in here and I was looking at a photo
… while I was looking at the picture, I felt 2 kicks on the ankle.
Johan: (SUBS) The child who walked past me here where I’m standing now is a child of about fifteen years old dressed in very dirty clothes…and he just disappeared into the wall….
Mac (SUBS) And you’re fine living here and coming in here?
Johan(SUBS) I’m so used to it… When I’m in another room for example, you will constantly hear things being moved around. And when you get back to the kitchen there is nothing, or a door that closes
Mac: Rather you than me.
Mac: There’s something special about these small towns and I can’t really put my finger on it. Is it the charm of the rustic old buildings? Is it the people? Or is it the environment? But Richmond touched a different kind of heartstring. It was really such a pleasant surprise seeing the horse museum, The library with all the history and the modern art. Really, really nice.

Loop Street with its picture perfect converted houses and B and B’s. There is a rich saddle horse history in the Richmond area. The earliest settlers, called Trekboers, had spent a lifetime in their saddles, and were among the best horsemen in the world. When diamonds were discovered, opportunities abounded for breeding carriage and draught horses, and for carting goods around the area. -The Horse Museum, in Loop Streett one of only two of its kind dedicated to the riding horse. . Johan Tolkien is the curator. Richmond was occupied by the English in the Anglo Boer war and under attack from Boer troops in Bloemfontein. Fort Vegkop , known to British as Flaghill to the Boers as Flagkop, Is the fort British soldiers would defend their occupation of Richmond. John Donaldson owner of Richmond Books and Prints – specialises in the history of the Anglo Boer War.
metadata.Further information: The nearest blockhouse is 40 kms away by Meriman Siding. ( Railway line). Right next door to the Horse Museum is another museum with a collection of interesting relics like, Anglo-Boer War gravestones; a relic from the old cooldrink factory; cuttings about an infamous local murder, a collection of vinyl albums of popular music from 50 years ago and an enormous whale vertebra, Further on along Loop Street is the reading room for the Bookbedonnerd Literary Festival, which takes place every October. The festival has featured literary notables like Athol Fugard; Professor Jonathan Jansen, Riaan Malan and Breyten Breytenbach over the past decade. A classic old brickworks, a bar with saddles for seats, Die Vetmuis restaurant started by four farm women and a Supper club, Die Supper Klub owned by a man who comes from Canada. With all that going on an extra ordinary feature of this little karoo dorp is the visually stunning MAPSA gallery with t’s large collection of modern and contemporary South African art. Part of the gallery is a book-binding centre, where a team of Richmond community women produce works of art in book form, using Japanese paper craft techniques to bind pages into books, covered in recycled flour, maize and sugar bags. ( if we send them our Carte Blanche logo they will create a wood cut) The brains behind this Modern Art Project is Harrie Siertsema and Pretoria-born, Berlin based artist and curator Abrie Fourie… both of them travel throughout the year but will be there on the May the first weekend. Another person who has found her own creative haven in the dorp is Lientjie Wessels, one of SA’s best chef’s or food artists . She will have a pop up food table on that weekend. Aubrey Williams and his husband created Karoo Creations during COVID when their Richmond Small Hotel was forced to shut it’s doors. To feed themselves and keep their staff in jobs they transformed their hotel into Karoo Creations, which produces top-end duvets made from sheep’s wool. “So, we were like, what can we do? Well we’re in the middle of sheep country, so we sourced around and found a supplier for wool that was still operating. We got a fabric supplier and started making duvets, and, ja, it took off like rockets At the edge of town is the Hope Centre, which feeds more than 200 Richmond children on most weekdays This is just a sample of what’s on offer in the dorp. The weekend 1st, 2nd and 3rd of May would be the perfect time to film, the town will be alive and vibrant with social and cultural hapenings and people. A good time for filming some essential interviews mixed with off the cuff people and events we come across.
